name: Alectinib
route_note: oral capsules 600 mg twice daily with food

discovery.note: A benzo[b]carbazolone ALK inhibitor active against crizotinib-resistant mutations and not a P-glycoprotein substrate, giving good brain penetration.

tagline: Brain-penetrant second-generation ALK inhibitor and first-line standard for ALK+ NSCLC
summary: Alectinib is a highly selective, brain-penetrant ALK inhibitor. It outperformed crizotinib as first-line therapy for ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, notably reducing brain progression, and in 2024 became the first ALK inhibitor approved as adjuvant therapy after surgery.
mechanism: Alectinib binds the ATP site of ALK and inhibits fusion kinases including many crizotinib-resistant mutants (L1196M, C1156Y, F1174L), blocking STAT3 and PI3K–AKT signalling.
Because it is not transported by P-glycoprotein efflux pumps, it reaches effective concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid; its major metabolite M4 is similarly active.
uses: First-line and post-crizotinib treatment of ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC
Adjuvant treatment after resection of ALK-positive NSCLC (stage IB–IIIA)

history.title: Preclinical report
history.detail: Chugai publishes CH5424802 as a selective ALK inhibitor (Cancer Cell).

history.title: Japan approval
history.detail: Approved in Japan for ALK-positive NSCLC.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: Approved for ALK-positive NSCLC after crizotinib.

history.title: ALEX
history.detail: ALEX shows superior progression-free survival over crizotinib; FDA approves first-line use.

history.title: ALINA
history.detail: FDA approves adjuvant alectinib after the ALINA trial reduced the risk of recurrence or death by about 76%.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4 to active metabolite M4

facts: In ALEX, the 12-month cumulative incidence of CNS progression was about 9% with alectinib versus 41% with crizotinib.
